answer: Sybil resistance rests on a deposit priced per identity. An agent must lock collateral worth a full participant share before mining or grading, so every extra identity costs the same stake as an honest one and stays exposed to slashing. Ten thousand clones tie up ten thousand stakes of idle, forfeitable capital, so cheap spam becomes an unhedged bet. Reputation compounds on the same horizon: payouts weight time served, so a clone starts at zero and waits out a long canyon of unpaid epochs. Attack cost grows linearly, honest yield does not, and no vine lets a clone skip the stake.
